title: Throw away a used fentanyl patch: fold it sticky sides together and post it into the locked drug drop box
instruction: Throw away his used fentanyl patch.
context: Fentanyl skin patches are worn by patients with severe chronic pain and are changed every three days, often by nurses, home-health aides and family carers. A used patch still holds a lethal dose for a child: "Even after a patch is used, there is enough fentanyl left to cause illness, overdose or death in babies, children, pets and others who are accidentally exposed" (FDA Consumer Update, Accidental Exposures to Fentanyl Patches Continue to Be Deadly to Children). The FDA therefore says: "The FDA recommends promptly disposing of used patches by folding them in half with the sticky sides together, and then flushing them down a toilet. Patches should not be placed in the household trash, where children or pets can find them." Done by: home health and personal care aides, nursing assistants and nurses, and family caregivers at home.
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. An older patient (a life-size adult mannequin in a polo shirt, fixed) sits at the robot's left end of the table (seat near x 48, y 97), facing along -y, his right forearm on the table. A bedside shelf (a dark walnut block 20 x 24 x 15 cm, fixed) stands in front of the robot: front edge at x 34.5, from y -22 to y 2. On its top lies the used patch, a Duragesic-style system: a thin, floppy, translucent near-colourless film 3.5 cm along x by 5 cm along y (0.2 mm thick, 4 g, sticky face up), printed in green with a 3 mm border, diagonal stripes and a name block in each half; its middle at x 35, y -12, its near end 1.2 cm out over the shelf's front edge; it bends anywhere across its width and folds in half along its middle line (along x, at y -12). On the shelf stand, fixed: a locked drug drop box (blue steel, 15 x 14.5 cm, 8 cm tall, centre x 46, y -14.25; a letter-box slot 6 x 3.2 cm in its lid at x 43.5, y -9.35, which a folded patch goes through but a flat one does not; inside, an anti-retrieval baffle: a 45-degree yellow ramp under the slot, 6.9 cm up at the box's far wall (y -7.4) down to the floor at its middle line (y -14.25), and a steel plate hanging from the lid across the box just past the slot's far edge (y -11.55 to -10.95, lower edge 4.0 cm above the floor), leaving a 5 mm throat square on to the ramp: a dropped patch slides down the ramp, under the plate, into a chamber beneath the solid lid; IEC 61032 test probe 19 (a child under 3's finger, 5.6 mm) does not pass the throat; a padlocked hasp on its front; a white DRUG DROP label on its lid, letters 3.75 cm tall) and an open grey household waste bin (inner 7 x 7 cm, 10 cm tall, centre x 49, y -2.5). Real trials: a care-training manikin; a fresh placebo training patch per trial (Wallcur Practi-Fentanyl Patch, #8100DF, or Pocket Nurse Demo Dose Fentynl 50 mcg/hr, PN01201), face up; gripper pads covered with PTFE tape changed each trial and wiped with isopropyl alcohol. Box: a lockable 1 mm steel cash box, padlocked, with a 60 x 32 mm slot cut in its lid (edges filed), the same label, a 1 mm aluminium ramp bent to 45 degrees, riveted in and lined with PTFE tape, and a 1 mm steel plate riveted under the lid just past the slot, the throat checked with a 5.6 mm pin gauge that must not pass; box and bin screwed to the shelf.
scoring: The patch counts as folded shut (stuck) once every part of one half lies face down on the matching part of the other, sticky faces together (within 9 mm and 25 degrees, touching); from then on it stays shut. Score 0 for the whole trial if any robot part comes within 4 cm of the patient. At the end: 1.0 only if, for the last 1 s, the patch has been folded shut, wholly in the locked drop box's chamber (down the baffle ramp and past the hanging plate, under the solid part of its lid), let go and at rest, which is also success; 0 otherwise: unfolded anywhere (even in the box), in the household bin, left folded on the shelf, on the box's lid, stuck in its slot, on the ramp or in the throat (where a hand could still reach it), still held, or off the shelf. Possible scores: 0, 1.0. On a real setup an overhead camera judges the fold and the posting, and the box is opened after the trial; a patch whose halves are not stuck together counts as unfolded.
reset_notes: Take the patch out of the box or bin (or use a fresh placebo patch, as on a real setup), unfold it flat (sticky face up) and lay it back on its mark with its near end 1.2 cm over the shelf's edge.
fidelity: The patch is ten rigid slats hinged edge to edge (1e-5 N m/rad springs; one PhysX articulation with self-collision, task-local hhpatch.py), bending at 5 mm spacing. It is 0.2 mm thick, about 4x a real Duragesic's 51 um, and 4 g, heavier than a real patch: both are chosen for a stable contact solve. Corners are square; the print is visual only. The adhesive is a switch that freezes the fold. The baffle is a fixed ramp and plate (mechkit.py). The patient is static.
scores: Scripted (yam_arena, 320x176, seed 0; dev GPU, 23 Nov 2026): demo 1.0 (step 657); naive 0.0; unsafe 0.0; short 0.0; idle 0.0. Dream-1 flash (seed 1) not yet run on this version; a Brev rerun is pending.
